extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy; practitioners interested in epistemology and method for inquiry
extracted.subtask_description: A classical philosophical method for attaining certain knowledge by systematic doubt, clear-and-distinct conception, and provisional practical maxims to live by while rebuilding belief. Includes rules for reasoning, preparation, and provisional conduct during inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the true order and enumerate all conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: “the method which teaches adherence to the true order, and an exact enumeration of all the conditions of the thing sought includes all that gives certitude to the rules of arithmetic.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct inquiry by following a strict, true order and by listing exhaustively the conditions of the object under investigation; this order and exact enumeration supply the certitude analogous to arithmetic. Anti-pattern: jumping steps or failing to list conditions leads to error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise reason universally to habituate clearer conceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the method not just for one subject but to exercise reason in all matters so the mind becomes 'gradually habituated to clearer and more distinct conceptions of its objects.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the method across domains to cultivate the habit of clear and distinct thinking. Example: practice the method on mathematical problems and then on other sciences. Avoid restricting the method to a single field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare by removing erroneous opinions and amassing experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Before undertaking the inquiry, eradicate from the mind erroneous opinions, amass a variety of experience to afford materials for reasonings, and continually exercise the method to increase skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical preparation involves self-critique, gathering empirical materials, and disciplined practice of method application. Anti-pattern: attempting radical reconstruction without prior preparation or experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain provisional maxims for practical living
rubrics_metrics.description: Form a provisory code of morals (three or four maxims) so one can live commodiously while suspending judgment during inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt temporary rules to guide behavior while engaging in radical doubt so as not to be paralysed in action. These maxims are practical placeholders, not final doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: First maxim: obey local laws, customs, and moderate opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: “to obey the laws and customs of my country, adhering firmly to the faith ... and regulating my conduct in every other matter according to the most moderate opinions ... of the most judicious of those among whom I might be living.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For practical affairs, follow prevailing moderate practices and the conduct of the most judicious in your community. Use observed practice rather than reported belief to ascertain opinions. Anti-pattern: immediately rejecting all communal norms and acting on isolated speculative judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer moderate opinions and observe practice over speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Among many opinions held in equal repute, choose the most moderate; determine others' real opinions by what they practise rather than what they say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting provisional beliefs, favor moderate stances (less distance from truth if wrong) and use behavior as the evidence of belief. Avoid extremes and literal adherence to promises that abridge freedom without reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second maxim: act resolutely on the most probable
rubrics_metrics.description: “to be as firm and resolute in my actions as I was able ... when it is not in our power to determine what is true, we ought to act according to what is most probable ... choose one or the other, and afterwards consider it ... as no longer dubious.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In matters of practice where truth is uncertain, pick the most probable option and treat it as certain for action to avoid indecision. Anti-pattern: perpetual hesitation or frequent switching of course for slight reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third maxim: change desires rather than the world; accept limits of control
rubrics_metrics.description: “to endeavor always to conquer myself rather than fortune, and change my desires rather than the order of the world ... except our own thoughts, there is nothing absolutely in our power.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate internal discipline and adjust desires to what is attainable. This reduces regret and fosters contentment. Requires prolonged discipline and meditation. Anti-pattern: attempting to control externals beyond one's power and persistent dissatisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make cultivation of reason one's chief occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: Continue devoting life to the culture of reason and making the greatest progress possible in the knowledge of truth via the prescribed method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize intellectual self-instruction and the steady practice of the method as the best life-project for attaining truth and virtue. Anti-pattern: substituting mere social or pleasurable occupations for disciplined intellectual work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological doubt: reject any opinion with the least ground for doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: “I ought to reject as absolutely false all opinions in regard to which I could suppose the least ground for doubt, in order to ascertain whether ... there remained aught in my belief that was wholly indubitable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ radical skepticism as a methodological tool: suspend belief in anything not absolutely indubitable, to discover secure foundations. Anti-pattern: treating skepticism as an end rather than a means to find certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept only what is clearly and distinctly perceived (cogito as first principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the indubitable truth of 'I think, therefore I am' and take as a general rule that 'all the things which we very clearly and distinctly conceive are true.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear-and-distinct perceptions as the criterion for truth; take the cogito as the foundational certainty from which to rebuild knowledge. Note caveats about properly determining which ideas are truly clear and distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace origin of ideas to determine their adequacy (causal/ontological considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When confronted with the idea of a more perfect being, conclude it must originate from a nature more perfect (God) rather than from oneself; use such causal reasoning to justify the existence of God and the reliability of clear ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an idea could arise from the subject's own imperfect nature; if not, infer a more adequate cause. Use these causal/ontological checks to underpin epistemic rules. Anti-pattern: accepting originless or self-explanatory ideas without causal scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege the understanding (reason) over imagination and senses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not be persuaded of the truth of anything unless on 'the evidence of our reason' rather than on imagination or sensory presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sensory and imaginative vividness as insufficient for truth; require rational evidence. Example: vivid dream images do not establish reality. Anti-pattern: conflating vivid imagination/sensation with demonstrative understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use simplified hypothetical models to deduce natural laws
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid scholastic disputes, consider what would happen in a new world created with minimal contentious assumptions and deduce laws of nature from those premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ thought-experiments or hypotheticals that minimize debated scholastic premises to make clear deductions about natural law. This strategy aims to produce explanations independent of prior contentious doctrines. Anti-pattern: entangling empirical theorizing in disputed prior authorities rather than isolating core laws.
